correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all 30 translated tetrahedra from the three stated difference cycles and all simplicial faces, obtaining f=(10,40,60,30). Fresh GF(2) linear algebra gives rank(d2)=30, rank(d3)=29 and H2 dimension one. Independent kernel lifting and rank-imaging for every one of the 1024 vertex subsets verifies r(S)=1 exactly when S contains a cyclic consecutive four-block, with zero mismatches. Independently all 210 four-subsets were checked: exactly ten missing tetrahedra, precisely the cyclic four-blocks. Exact support-layer counts 4:10,5:50,6:100,7:100,8:45,9:10,10:1; every eight-subset qualifies and an explicit seven-subset has no four-block. This exhausts the stated finite object without relying on stored VERIFY_OK output or any extrapolation.
residual_risks: Calculation is only for the specified cyclic 10-vertex complex over F2, not an infinite family or integral result.

value.rationale: The cyclic 10-vertex triangulation of S2×S1 is a natural minimal-dimensional combinatorial-manifold test object, and the image-support ideal of induced H2 into global H2 is a motivated local-to-global invariant. The complete exact counts at every vertex cardinality, ten minimal missing-tetrahedron carriers and sharp forced-surjectivity threshold eight supply structural information not implied numerically by global Betti numbers or a generic enumeration of faces. A later researcher studying induced homology, tightness or vertex-support systoles could use the full exact spectrum. No general family theorem is required for this precisely characterized finite invariant.
residual_risks: Object-specific numerical classification has limited generality; cannot infer other triangulations or coefficients.
The larger finite census remains bounded to ten vertices; value is the natural exact invariant rather than a claimed landmark theorem.

limitations: Classification is only for specified labelled cyclic 10-vertex triangulation and mod-2 coefficients; no all-parameter conclusion.
Some exact-object primary sources could not be read in full; best-of-knowledge originality is not exhaustive priority certification.
